title: BEST APP EVER INVENTED!!!
body:
I cannot emphasize enough how transformative Habbit Rabbit has been for my daily life. This app isn't just about forming habits; it's about revolutionizing your entire routine with an adorable and interactive twist. Here's why Habbit Rabbit stands head and shoulders above the rest:

Engaging and Motivational: Habbit Rabbit turns habit tracking into a fun and engaging game. Every task you complete helps your virtual rabbit grow and thrive, making you eager to keep up with your goals. The sense of accomplishment you get from seeing your rabbit flourish is unparalleled.

User-Friendly Interface: The app's design is sleek, intuitive, and incredibly user-friendly. Even if you're new to habit tracking, Habbit Rabbit makes it easy to get started and stay organized. The visuals are delightful, and the animations add a touch of magic to your daily routine.

Customization and Personalization: Habbit Rabbit allows you to customize your experience to suit your unique needs. You can set personalized goals, track various habits, and receive tailored reminders. The app adapts to your lifestyle, ensuring that you stay on track no matter how busy you are.

Community and Support: The Habbit Rabbit community is vibrant and supportive. You can connect with other users, share your progress, and get inspired by their achievements. The app also offers plenty of resources and tips to help you overcome challenges and stay motivated.

Incredible Results: Since I started using Habbit Rabbit, I've noticed a significant improvement in my productivity, health, and overall well-being. The app's positive reinforcement and gamified approach have helped me build and maintain habits that I struggled with for years.

Adorable Graphics: Let's not forget the star of the show - the rabbit! The app's adorable graphics and animations make habit tracking a delightful experience. Watching your rabbit grow and evolve as you complete tasks is incredibly satisfying and keeps you coming back for more.

In conclusion, Habbit Rabbit is not just an app; it's a lifestyle enhancer. It has transformed my approach to habit building and made achieving my goals fun and rewarding. If you're looking for a way to improve your daily routine and stay motivated, look no further than Habbit Rabbit. Download it now and watch your life change for the better!

title: Super cute and helpful! 🐰💖… Only one problem…
body:
I’ve only used this app for 2 to 3 days, and I found it really helpful! I mean, it’s still really early for me to see improvement for myself to make more healthier habits, but at least it’s really helpful that every time I see the app, I think, “Oh, I should really read,” or “I should really do my homework.” And I’m sure that will eventually lead to to me actually taking action on those habits and making improvement 😊

Plus, it’s really cute with the rabbit and the style of art in this app! I like how you can journal in the app, and pick a face to represent what you felt from the day. Also, I think it’s adorable the fact that the rabbit will encourages you to do the habits! 🐰💕

So, the reason why I didn’t rate it 5 stars is because it takes way too much of my battery power in such of a short time. After about 10 minutes of using it, the power was from 80 percent to 30 percent. And my phone was really warm. So, I have to use this app really quickly to save power.
I’m not quite sure why this happens with this specific app. Anyway, I hope it can be somehow solved.

Thank you for reading my review.

title: Bad for ADHD - Has Potential
body:
I have Finch and was considering switching because with Finch you can only auto-sync one device, Habit Rabbit you can sync multiple devices. I had Study Bunny for exactly 30 minutes before deleting it. There is an ad after every, single, tiny, thing you do. The ads are over bearing and are a major distraction and frustration. Unlike the creator’s other app, Study Bunny, there is no $2.00 30-day trial to take the ads down and see if you like it. You’d have to pay at least $10 to just give it a fair shot, considering most other apps make a 7 or 30-day trial free… that’s audacious. 

I kinda vibe with the simplicity of the art style and the idea that the bunny can get sad. The bird in Finch is always just happy you’re back - it’s a reward only system rather than reward/punishment - some people won’t like that at all so Habit Rabbit has that going for it in addition to the multiple device capabilities. I almost just paid the $15 out of curiosity, excitement, and frustration, BUT I invested the app more. Even with premium, there is also no categorization other than “priority” and no recurrence assignment other than weekly. 

I can’t say poking around this app was a waste of time because now I am just going to assume if an app is extremely restrictive on the free tier yet can’t even give you at bare minimum 3-days of premium free, that’s a red flag, but if there’s not even a dirt cheap 30-day trial, that’s a full STOP sign. This app needs major work to compete with its competitors.

title: Limited and Distracting
body:
The app is cute and simple, which I like. Complexity takes attention away from the point - tracking habits. However, the app did not give a tutorial to move through it and I found myself experiencing a steep learning curve with all the unlabeled icons to access checklists and habits. 

Also, right out of the gate, after the app made it clear that the game is to collect carrots by completing tasks and reinforcing good habits, it gave me a hook of watching ads for carrots. This is offered 3 times a day, offering double or triple rewards if done more than once consecutively. This feels totally counterintuitive and absolutely distracting. I want to do beneficial things in real life to earn rewards, not distract myself with mindless ads.

There are also short ads built into the app, which I guess is ok since it’s free. 

Another issue is that you can’t set more than 1 high priority goal and no more than 3 medium priority goals in the free version. Not worth it, in my opinion. There are many others out there, Habitica being a really good option for one.

title: It’s good! (READ)
body:
If you’re looking for something simple yet motivating this is for you! 

It’s a cute theme with peaceful music in the back. it makes it feel like all your habits are going to be just fine <3 instead of it feeling like work.
     You can unlock other areas for your rabbit friend and buy cats dogs and Squirrels (etc) to go along with the carrots you get by completing your tasks.
    
You can also track your moods for each day which has helped me a TON!! I’m so thankful for that little detail.
   You can also track your steak which helps motivate you sometimes.
    If you just like being organized with not too much on your plate this is a great way to start ☺️

    The reason I only gave it three stars is because you have to pay to get more habits. I think you get  eight habits total, which is a good amount however I wish there was more. It make sense for the company to do so, since they need money but you get an ad almost every time you complete a task.
     That’s probably the biggest reason, I do wish you could add little side quests towards your main one

For example, I could put down drawing and be able to have an option to attach another habit onto that such as;
     Anatomy,
     Free drawing,
     Study,
     Color theory,
     Painting
  Etc.

A possible update advice but other than that if you don’t mind the limited habits then this is a great place to be!!
   If you’re more serious about them then you could still have this but maybe find something a little more specific. 

Hope this helped!

title: Useful
body:
This app is incredibly helpful. I find it’s “free tier” usage incredibly wide compared to other trackers (ie, some other apps have ridiculously low limits on the amount of habits you can track daily, and expect ludicrous payments for their premium tiers to track more habits). It is also incredibly cute, and the motivation to keep my rabbit’s room tidy and nice keeps me pushing through my habits. 
My only complaint is that the app was very confusing for me to figure out. The tutorial is brief, and doesn’t show nearly half of the functions the app has, including the most important one : how to add and delete habits. I spent a good 15 minutes trying to find that specific function. As a suggestion, I would suggest either making the tutorial more expansive, or having users complete a tour/guide of the app upon first download. Just something that points out what’s what, and highlights the most useful functions.
Otherwise, I think the app is genius, and I am happy to have found it.

body:
This app low key changed my life. I’ve tried SO MANY habit trackers but for some reason cleaning this stupid bunny’s stupid room is what finally got me to stick to one (i use the term stupid lovingly). 

I’ve spent money on this app SOLELY to support the developer because I can’t thank him (Justin???) enough for making this app.

 this app was a mAJOR TOOL for me when i was trying to go from waking up at noon to waking up at 6 in the morning and going to the gym. When I want to skip washing my face at night I go “hmmm well if i dont, i wont be able to log my habbit, and i won’t reach the goal i set for this week and also my bunmy will be sad” so i just ??? wash my face ?? it was that easy this WHOLE time ?? 

A simple app, made with love, and it freaking works for some reason.

IMPROVEMENT SUGGESTIONS:
- So right now your deleted habits don’t save. This honestly isn’t a big deal but I really like the feature where you can go back in time and see how you did hitting your habits for a month. It will say 0% completion for any habit that you added after that month, and won’t show how you did for the habits you had at the time. Having each months habits saved even after deletion would be great for those whose habits change often. 

- Im close to finishing cleaning the bunnies rooms. A lot of people asked for more rooms which would ALSO be good but here me out: being able to reset the bunnies house and make it dirty again. Keep track of how many times the user has reset so they can look and use that as a measure of progress. Almost like a prestige in call of duty. This is allows users to feel like their making progress towards a goal while they wait for more rooms to get added (if that’s in the plan). 

These suggestions aren’t even that crucial but just thought I would throw some thoughts your way!

title: The only productivity app I like.
body:
I’ve tried a lot of productivity/habit-building apps. This is the ONLY one I’ve stuck with. Not only that, but I genuinely enjoy using it. The personalization (naming/customization of rabbit and their home) and aesthetic UI make me want to come back every day. But what really makes it work is the carefully crafted gamification. 

It manages to toe the delicate lines between simplicity and longevity. It’s simple enough to quickly check off habits throughout the day. The rewards are numerous enough and balanced just right so that you can see significant progress with every habit checked, but it isn’t too fast (or too slow). 

I’ve used Habit Rabbit for two weeks now and I have already built several habits into my routine that I’ve otherwise struggled to do routinely - for YEARS. (Flossed every night this week instead of putting it off because I could always do it tomorrow instead. Cleaned the dishes and put them away as I used them instead of letting them pile up in the sink.)

Whether you want to start something new or hold yourself accountable for things you currently struggle with, GET THIS LIL RABBIT.

title: Good, but Bug?
body:
Now, the three stars is for a potential bug. There is no way to turn off notifications if you set them up. When you press on a habit, it takes you to the screen with the habit info. Then press the bell and that brings you to the notifications. Now, it has a little button you press at the top for notifications, that I assume turns off the notifications, but it doesn't work. 

 I love the app. I use it almost every day! It lets you see this week and last weeks' progress in habit formation. It also records statistically how many habits you complete monthly. I think it's very helpful for keeping on track. Plus, seeing your progress is such a great motivator to keep your streak up! And decorating the rabbit's house is a cute and fun little project. It is extremely satisfying to completely clean up a room. 

 As a suggestion, maybe every week or day a new mess appears in a random completed room? Because habits require upkeep, like the rabbit's house. I haven't quite finished the last room, but there doesn't seem to be a lot of uses for the coins you build up, when you get to the end. So maybe adding some random tidy-up tasks could help. 

 I used vacation mode several times in the past two months, but I still kept up with some habits. I wanted to keep up my streak even though I was "on vacation". Your health and levels don't deplete during vacation mode, so you get the 100% health bonus when the mode is turned on. I don't think so many coins should accrue during vacation mode. It feels like cheating to me. I accrued so many coins just with maintaining my habits that I feel like I undermined my progress so far. I did everything I could for a couple months to earn coins to clean up previous rooms, but in the past week I earned several hundred coins just by keeping vacation mode on and doing only 2 habits. I feel cheated because it was so easy earning coins while keeping vacation mode on, so why was I putting in so much effort earlier? Anyway, thank you for the app and I look forward to your next updates!
